population: U.S. adults 18+ recruited with consent and appropriate human-subject review

factors.name: partisan_identity
factors.note: Cue relative to respondent's prior party identification; independents must be prespecified as distinct/handled through explicit exclusion with disclosure

hypothesis: Delivery style influences perceived authenticity; effects may differ by partisan congruence
primaryOutcome: Validated perceived political authenticity measure; use and scoring require instrument/license review

stimulus.scenario: Fictional congressional candidate answering a question about spending transparency
stimulus.high: Our commitment is to accountability, transparency, and results. We will hold quarterly public meetings, publish spending records within 30 days, and publicly explain delays.
stimulus.low: You should be able to see where the money goes. I'd meet with people every quarter, put the spending records online within 30 days, and explain any delays.
stimulus.note: Both original, fictitious scripts; pretest that factual commitments and perceived competence are balanced before fielding; do not claim real politician speech.

randomization: Computer-generated block randomization within preregistered party strata; allocation audit before human contact
analysis: Intention-to-treat regression with both factors, interaction, prespecified controls, design weights if appropriate, 95% CIs, multiplicity correction on secondary outcomes
publicationWarning: Protocol completion does not validate a causal experiment; do not present treatment effects until actual consented randomized responses are analyzed
